subject: Pricing for structured JSON output + tool/function calling — rate card & metering impact
messages:
From: Maya Srinivasan <maya@atlashealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Pricing for structured/tool calls (JSON mode) and metering impact

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for taking this — AtlasHealth is evaluating Redwood for a patient-data ingestion pipeline where we need a high volume of structured JSON responses and occasional tool calls to a record-enrichment service. Before we jump into a demo, can you share the hosted API rate card that shows how you meter:

- per-token usage (in/out)
- function/tool calling (are calls billed per invocation?)
- structured output / "JSON mode" — is there an additional surcharge or different metering?

For context, our expected PoC profile: ~100k API requests/day, average prompt 80 tokens, expected structured JSON output ~200 tokens, and ~0.2 function calls per request (some requests trigger 1–2 enrichment calls). We're trying to model TCO.

Two asks:
1) Can you provide baseline hosted pricing + any committed-use discount tiers?
2) If you can, run a sample cost calc for the numbers above (we're trying to compare to our existing provider).

We may also be able to commit to 12 months if the economics work — target net discount in the 30% range from list.

I've attached a short PoC spec (internal).

Thanks,
Maya
Maya Srinivasan
Director, Platform Integrations
AtlasHealth

Attachment: atlas_poc_spec.pdf (see attached)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya@atlashealth.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 12:05:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Pricing for structured/tool calls (JSON mode) and metering impact

Hi Maya — great to meet you over email. Short answers up front, then a few pricing bullets and next steps.

Summary (hosted API, list):
- Token metering: billed per input and output token; list baseline is $0.0006 per input token and $0.0010 per output token.
- Function / tool calls: billed per invocation at $0.0020 per call (this covers the extra routing, logs, and per-call quota accounting). Each model-initiated invocation counts as one billable call.
- Structured output (JSON mode): charged as normal token usage + a validation surcharge of +20% on the output token portion when output_mode=json (this covers schema validation, strict parsing, and structured safety checks).

Committed-use discount examples (hosted):
- 10% off list at $50k/mo commit
- 25% off list at $150k/mo commit
- 40% off list at $400k/mo commit

Quick calc for your PoC profile (rough):
- Requests/day: 100k
- Prompt tokens (in): 80 * 100k = 8M tokens/day
- Output tokens (json): 200 * 100k = 20M tokens/day
- Token cost/day (list): (8M * $0.0006) + (20M * $0.0010) = $4,800 + $20,000 = $24,800/day -> $744k/month (30 days)
- JSON surcharge (20% on output tokens): 20M * $0.0010 * 0.20 = $4,000/day -> $120k/mo
- Function calls: 0.2 * 100k = 20k calls/day -> 20k * $0.002 = $40/day -> $1,200/mo
- Total hosted list estimate: ~$865k/mo (includes token + JSON surcharge + calls)

That obviously needs tailoring — e.g., average output token length, batching, and KV/prefix caching can dramatically reduce token cost. We also often recommend:
- Prefix caching for repeated prompts (common for HL7-like templated requests)
- Aggressive batching for backfill parts of pipeline
- Offloading enrichment to a cached microservice so tool calls are less frequent

Attachments: I'm attaching a short rate card PDF and a quick calc spreadsheet so you can swap in different numbers (redwood_quick_calc.xlsx).

If you're targeting ~30% net to list, we can get there with a 12-month committed ARR arrangement. Example: a $300k/mo committed level would map to roughly 30–35% off list. If you want I can loop in Marcus (our Pricing Lead) and produce a formal committed quote and draft SOW/DocuSign.

Would you be available for a follow-up call Thursday?

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Account Executive — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_rate_card_q1_2026.pdf, redwood_quick_calc.xlsx

From: Maya Srinivasan <maya@atlashealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 08:23:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Pricing for structured/tool calls (JSON mode) and metering impact

Thanks, Soojin — very helpful. A few clarifying q's:

1) JSON surcharge: is that applied to every response where output_mode=json, even when the structured payload is small (e.g., single field)? Do you offer a per-response floor instead?
2) Tool calls: we have enrichment flows where a single user request may fan out to 3 external API calls (model triggers tool A -> tool B chained). Do you bill per model->tool invocation in that chain?
3) Dedicated vs Hosted: Are the hosted list numbers above comparable to Dedicated committed pricing, or do Dedicated contracts have a different model (flat GPU seat + lower per-token charges)?

Also — our procurement team made it clear: to get to a 30% net we need the combination of committed discount + an initial PoC credit. Is Redwood able to offer a short-term credit (we were thinking $15k) that can be applied against the first 60 days while we ramp to committed usage?

If you can answer those and share a formal committed quote, we can loop in legal/procurement.

Thanks,
Maya

(On behalf of Procurement: procurement@atlashealth.com)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya@atlashealth.com>, Procurement <procurement@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 10:45:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Pricing for structured/tool calls (JSON mode) and metering impact

Hi Maya / Procurement team — looping Marcus on the pricing specifics. Answers inline: 

1) JSON surcharge: applied when output_mode=json on the response. It scales with the output_token count (we apply the 20% uplift to the output token subtotal). We do not currently have a per-response floor for the surcharge, but we can negotiate an exception for very small/low-volume responses as part of a committed contract.

2) Tool calls & chaining: yes, every model-initiated invocation is billed as a separate call. So in your chained example (A -> B), if the model triggers two invocations that we route/track, that's two billable calls. We can discuss an inclusive bundle (e.g., first X calls per request or per-100 requests included) as part of a committed tier.

3) Dedicated vs Hosted: Dedicated is structured differently — typically a committed monthly capacity fee (GPU seats or throughput units) plus lower per-token and per-call unit rates. The economics are usually better for sustained, very high-throughput customers, but there is an operational minimum and a longer procurement cycle. I can put together a side-by-side hosted vs dedicated cost model.

PoC credit: we can offer a $15k credit applied to the first 60 days contingent on signing a 12-month committed ARR at ~$300k/mo (example structure). That nets to roughly the 30% goal you mentioned. I'll prepare a formal committed quote and SOW draft for legal.

Next steps I propose: 
- Marcus will put together the committed quote + a short addendum that describes an inclusive tool-call bundle (example: 1 included call per request, additional calls at $0.0008/call in committed tier).
- I'll share a DocuSign-enabled quote and the rate card PDF.
- Schedule a 30-min alignment call next week to finalize numbers.

Marcus, could you review the attached draft rate card and confirm whether we can include the 1-call-per-request bundle and the $15k PoC credit structure?

Thanks all,
— Soojin

Redwood Inference
